checks: A representative of each maximal minimal face can be chosen in its relative interior by the definition of a minimal face. A same-parity pair has an integer midpoint in the complete I. Every face containing that midpoint contains both endpoints, hence both minimal faces. Distinct maximal minimal faces therefore have disjoint representative parities, including for arbitrary relative-interior representatives.

At m=k(I), every z has the parity of a unique p_i. Its midpoint with p_i has a minimal face containing F_i, hence F_i by maximality. The midpoint lies in relint(F_i) and can have no other representative's parity. Iteration gives p_i+2^(−j)(z−p_i) integral for every j. Thus each coordinate of z−p_i is divisible by every power of two, so z=p_i.

Every vertex of Q is in I. A positive-dimensional F_i would contain a vertex distinct from its relative-interior representative. That vertex would be another p_j, and its singleton face would contradict maximality. Conversely parity-distinct vertices yield exactly k(I) singleton faces, and extremality excludes nontrivial anchored representations. A singleton base obeys all these claims.

The actual buffered cover in the proof of 088f4667ef9ef0b0 chooses exactly every maximal minimal face. Its complete I gives m≤k(I)≤k(P); equality at the ends gives the desired contact census. In a lower-rank saturated affine lattice, a coordinate half-difference of two sites that is integral lies in the direction space, so inherited and original parities agree.
Original c3bb7df3660a88b5 §§1 and 5 have the same equality statement and buffered contact conclusion. The archived exact face replay passed 50,334 checks on 1,690 complete planar lattice hulls.

dependencies.mapping: For the application only, use the complete maximizing I and the explicitly chosen maximal minimal faces of conv(I) from the fixed invariant buffer theorem under its shifted-own-section hypotheses. The contact sets there are exactly I∩F_i and its occupied-parity budget is k(P).

overlap.comparison: Its cover proof already selects the maximal occupied faces and establishes the count m≤k(I)≤k(P). It does not classify equality or prove that every old contact set is a singleton at full budget.

Its exceptional parity-distinct-vertex configuration also imposes equal weights and concerns the strict mass of a chosen minimal face. It does not prove equality classification for the number of all maximal minimal faces.

readability: The equality characterization concerns the chosen maximal minimal faces and their old contact sets. It makes no assertion about all exposed faces of an arbitrary corrected resultant.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The occupied-parity count and its equality characterization hold for all finite complete lattice bases, including rank zero. Equality makes the actual buffered contact sets singletons under the stated predecessor setup.
